diagnostic_approaches.name: ASA Difficult Airway Definition
criteria_or_scoring: “the clinical situation in which a conventionally trained anesthesiologist experiences difficulty with face mask ventilation
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: If difficulty with mask ventilation or tracheal intubation occurs, classify as a difficult airway.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When assessing airway difficulty in patients
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A difﬁcult airway is “the clinical situation in which a conventionally trained anesthesiologist experiences difﬁculty with face mask ventilation, difﬁculty with tracheal intubation, or both” [1].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Palpation via thyroid notch to identify cricothyroid membrane
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify the cricothyroid membrane for airway access
criteria_or_scoring: Located inferior to thyroid cartilage border and superior to cricoid cartilage
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Slide a finger down the thyroid cartilage to identify the membrane position between cartilages.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Membrane is identified when palpated between thyroid and cricoid cartilages.
limitations: In patients with significant neck edema or trauma
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Before cricothyroidotomy to locate the CT membrane
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: sliding a ﬁnger down the thyroid cartilage, the cricothyroid membrane can be identiﬁed just inferior to the border of this cartilage and superior to the cricoid cartilage

diagnostic_approaches.name: Alternative landmark: suprasternal notch distance to CT membrane
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate CT membrane location when landmarks are difficult to palpate
criteria_or_scoring: Suprasternal notch is typically three to four fingerbreadths below the CT membrane
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use suprasternal notch and measure three to four fingerbreadths upward with the neck neutral.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: CT membrane lies three to four fingerbreadths above the suprasternal notch.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When edema, trauma, or obesity obscures anterior neck landmarks
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: An alternative landmark is the suprasternal notch, which is typically three to four ﬁngerbreadths below the CT membrane with the neck in neutral position.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Syringe aspiration air bubbles to confirm CT membrane puncture
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm airway entry during needle cricothyroidotomy
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Advance needle at a 45° angle pointing inferiorly; aspirate to detect air bubbles after passing the CT membrane.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Air bubbles in the syringe indicate entry into the airway.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During needle cricothyroidotomy to verify placement
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: advanced through the skin at a 45° angle pointing inferiorly. When the needle pushes through the CT membrane, aspiration will reveal air bubbles within the syringe.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Three-finger laryngeal stabilization and CT membrane palpation
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Locate and reidentify the CT membrane during surgical cricothyroidotomy
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Immobilize larynx with thumb and long finger; use index finger to palpate and reidentify the CT membrane.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Tactile confirmation of CT membrane location.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the larynx is ﬁrmly immobilized by the thumb and long ﬁnger, with the index ﬁnger free to palpate, locate, and reidentify the cricothyroid (CT) membrane

diagnostic_approaches.name: Palpation of cricothyroid (CT) membrane through incision
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Reconfirm CT membrane position before proceeding
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Index finger palpates the CT membrane through the incision while larynx is pinned in midline.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: After skin incision while stabilizing larynx.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the index finger palpates the CT membrane through the incision, reconfirming its position and planning the following steps.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Capnography (CO2 return) to confirm tube placement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm proper placement of tracheostomy or endotracheal tube
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use monitoring equipment to detect CO2 return.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Before securing tube to neck with suture.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: proper placement should be confirmed by both the presence of CO2 return on the monitoring equipment and successful auscultation of breath sounds.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Auscultation of breath sounds to confirm tube placement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm proper placement of tracheostomy or endotracheal tube
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Auscultate for breath sounds after tube insertion.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Before securing tube to neck with suture.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: proper placement should be confirmed by both the presence of CO2 return on the monitoring equipment and successful auscultation of breath sounds.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Aspiration of air via syringe during percutaneous cricothyroidotomy
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm proper needle position within the airway
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Introduce an 18-gauge needle with syringe through the CT membrane; confirm by aspirating air.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During percutaneous cricothyroidotomy after landmark identification and laryngeal fixation.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: an 18-gauge needle attached to a syringe is introduced through the CT membrane, and proper positioning is confirmed with aspiration of air.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Point-of-care ultrasound to identify the cricothyroid membrane
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify CT membrane anatomy prior to cricothyroidotomy
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use handheld point-of-care ultrasound in the emergency setting.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Using point-of-care ultrasound can identify the cricothyroid membrane prior to cricothyroidotomy and potentially decrease complications.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Flexible endoscopy or formal bronchoscopy after surgical access
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Examine the airway for causes of obstruction
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform flexible endoscopy or formal bronchoscopy after access is stabilized.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Identifies airway pathology; reversible causes can then be addressed.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the airway should be examined either by flexible endoscopy or formal bronchoscopy.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Postoperative chest x-ray
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Identifies presence or absence of pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Postoperative chest x-ray is important to rule out pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.

treatment_algorithms.title: Surgical airway as final common pathway on difficult airway algorithms
specific_recommendations: The surgical airway remains the final common pathway on all difficult airway algorithms, and cricothyroidotomy is an effective technique if emergency invasive airway access is required.
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: The surgical airway remains the final common pathway on all difficult airway algorithms, and cricothyroidotomy is an effective technique if emergency invasive airway access is required.

treatment_algorithms.title: Cricothyroidotomy in Difficult Airway Algorithms and Elective Use
treatment_algorithms.condition: Difficult airway management; elective airway access decisions
specific_recommendations: Cricothyroidotomy offers the quickest route to stabilizing the airway and should be the first-line therapy in emergent settings.
As an elective procedure, cricothyroidotomy is only appropriate in some cases, notably in those without antecedent intubation or laryngeal pathology.
decision_points_and_pathways: Emergent setting: prioritize cricothyroidotomy as first-line therapy.
Elective setting: consider only in selected patients (no antecedent intubation or laryngeal pathology).
treatment_algorithms.patient_population_criteria: Elective candidates most notably without antecedent intubation or laryngeal pathology.
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: cricothyroidotomy offers the quickest route to stabilizing the airway and should be the ﬁrst-line therapy.

clinical_guidelines.title: ASA 2003 consensus: Surgical airway endpoint in emergency difficult airway
specific_recommendations: The 2003 American Society of Anesthesiologists consensus statement confirms surgical airway as the endpoint for unsuccessful airway control in an emergency setting [1].
As soon as an inability to intubate and ventilate is determined, surgical airway access should be pursued; continued attempts at intubation increases morbidity and mortality.
decision_points_and_pathways: If inability to intubate and ventilate is determined, proceed to surgical airway.
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: continued attempts at intubation increases morbidity and mortality
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The 2003 American Society of Anesthesiologists consensus statement confirms surgical airway as the endpoint for unsuccessful airway control in an emergency setting [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: ASA practice guidelines: Definition of difficult airway
specific_recommendations: A difficult airway is “the clinical situation in which a conventionally trained anesthesiologist experiences difficulty with face mask ventilation, difficulty with tracheal intubation, or both” [1].
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A difficult airway is “the clinical situation in which a conventionally trained anesthesiologist experiences difficulty with face mask ventilation, difficulty with tracheal intubation, or both” [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: Primary indication for emergent surgical airway
specific_recommendations: The primary indication for an emergent surgical airway is the failure of endotracheal intubation or noninvasive airway maneuvers in a patient requiring immediate airway control.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The primary indication for an emergent surgical airway is the failure of endotracheal intubation or noninvasive airway maneuvers in a patient requiring immediate airway control.

clinical_guidelines.title: Pediatric contraindication to surgical cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: A strong contraindication to surgical cricothyroidotomy is age less than 10 years.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: needle cricothyroidotomy with percutaneous transtracheal ventilation
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A strong contraindication to surgical cricothyroidotomy is age less than 10 years.

clinical_guidelines.title: Preferred emergency airway in children: needle cricothyroidotomy (10–12 years threshold)
specific_recommendations: In children younger than 10–12 years, needle cricothyroidotomy is the preferred method for establishing an emergency airway, since the CT membrane is small and can be difficult to locate quickly.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Surgical cricothyroidotomy may easily damage the larynx in this age group
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: needle cricothyroidotomy with percutaneous transtracheal ventilation
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In children younger than 10–12 years, needle cricothyroidotomy is the preferred method for establishing an emergency airway, since the CT membrane is small and can be difficult to locate quickly.

clinical_guidelines.title: Avoid elective cricothyroidotomy after prolonged intubation or laryngeal inflammation/trauma
specific_recommendations: it is advisable to avoid cricothyroidotomy as an elective procedure in patients intubated for longer than 5–7 days, if laryngeal inflammation or infection is present, or there is history of laryngeal trauma.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: patients intubated for longer than 5–7 days; laryngeal inflammation or infection; history of laryngeal trauma
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: prolonged intubation; laryngeal inflammation or infection; history of laryngeal trauma
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: it is advisable to avoid cricothyroidotomy as an elective procedure in patients intubated for longer than 5–7 days, if laryngeal inflammation or infection is present, or there is history of laryngeal trauma.

clinical_guidelines.title: Relative contraindications to surgical cricothyroidotomy; consider lower tracheostomy
specific_recommendations: Relative contraindications for surgical cricothyroidotomy include severe neck trauma or edema and expanding neck hematoma.
Known upper tracheal pathology is another relative contraindication.
If a true anatomic barrier exists, then a lower tracheostomy may be the only viable option to secure the airway.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: severe neck trauma or edema; expanding neck hematoma; known upper tracheal pathology
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Relative contraindications for surgical cricothyroidotomy include severe neck trauma or edema and expanding neck hematoma. Known upper tracheal pathology is another relative contraindication.

clinical_guidelines.title: Needle cricothyroidotomy: oxygen flow and CO2 release
specific_recommendations: oxygen can be delivered at a high flow rate of 10–12 l/min.
Use of a Y-connector will allow periodic release of some carbon dioxide [13].
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: periodic release of some carbon dioxide via Y-connector
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: oxygen can be delivered at a high flow rate of 10–12 l/min. Use of a Y-connector will allow periodic release of some carbon dioxide [13].

clinical_guidelines.title: Needle cricothyroidotomy in young children: convert to tracheostomy
specific_recommendations: In young children, needle cricothyroidotomy should be converted to tracheostomy as soon as feasible.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In young children, needle cricothyroidotomy should be converted to tracheostomy as soon as feasible.

clinical_guidelines.title: Surgical cricothyroidotomy: skin incision length and placement
specific_recommendations: a 2-cm midline vertical skin incision centered over the CT membrane is made, avoiding injury to the anterior jugular veins (Fig. 3b).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: a 2-cm midline vertical skin incision centered over the CT membrane is made, avoiding injury to the anterior jugular veins (Fig. 3b).

clinical_guidelines.title: Surgical cricothyroidotomy: neck preparation, positioning, and landmark identification
specific_recommendations: Positioning for cricothyroidotomy differs than that for tracheostomy, as it is more important for the patient’s mandible to be anteriorly displaced than for the neck to be extended, as in tracheostomy.
Palpation and identification of external landmarks including thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage, and sternal notch is a critical first step.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Palpation and identification of external landmarks including thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage, and sternal notch is a critical first step.

clinical_guidelines.title: Emergency tracheostomy risk compared with cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: It should be noted that emergency tracheostomy or the so-called slash trach does carry a higher risk of complication than cricothyroidotomy.
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: higher risk of complication with emergency tracheostomy
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: It should be noted that emergency tracheostomy or the so-called slash trach does carry a higher risk of complication than cricothyroidotomy.

clinical_guidelines.title: Needle cricothyroidotomy is temporizing in adults
clinical_guidelines.condition: Adult emergency airway via needle cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: the catheter is usually too small to provide adequate ventilation other than as a temporizing measure; typically, needle cricothyroidotomy is only used in preparation for either surgical cricothyroidotomy or tracheostomy.
Though oxygen can be delivered by this method, there is limited ability to actively eliminate carbon dioxide.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: limited ability to actively eliminate carbon dioxide
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the catheter is usually too small to provide adequate ventilation other than as a temporizing measure; typically, needle cricothyroidotomy is only used in preparation for either surgical cricothyroidotomy or tracheostomy.

clinical_guidelines.title: Alternative landmark when CT membrane not palpable
specific_recommendations: An alternative landmark is the suprasternal notch, which is typically three to four fingerbreadths below the CT membrane with the neck in neutral position.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: An alternative landmark is the suprasternal notch, which is typically three to four fingerbreadths below the CT membrane with the neck in neutral position.

clinical_guidelines.title: Preferred site within CT membrane for incision
specific_recommendations: For this reason, incision within the CT membrane should be made in the lower half.
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: reduced bleeding risk from cricothyroid arteries
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For this reason, incision within the CT membrane should be made in the lower half.

clinical_guidelines.title: Avoid anterior jugular vein injury during cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: Anterior jugular veins can be avoided by making a vertical incision in the skin and staying in the midline during the procedure.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Anterior jugular veins can be avoided by making a vertical incision in the skin and staying in the midline during the procedure.

clinical_guidelines.title: Standard Open Surgical Cricothyroidotomy – Exposure, Dilation, and Cannula Insertion
specific_recommendations: Make a horizontal incision through the lower border of the cricothyroid membrane to avoid injury to superiorly positioned vessels.
Insert a cricoid hook and apply gentle upward traction; prefer hooking the cricoid to avoid vocal fold injury.
Dilate the CT membrane incision in a cephalocaudal direction with a Trousseau dilator or Kelly clamp.
Use a tracheostomy or endotracheal tube with outer diameter not exceeding 8 mm.
Confirm tube placement by presence of CO2 return and successful auscultation of breath sounds before securing.
decision_points_and_pathways: Localize CT membrane and perform horizontal incision at lower border.
Insert cricoid hook; apply upward traction to bring airway closer to skin.
Dilate cephalocaudally to enlarge airway opening.
Insert tested cannula/tube and confirm placement (CO2 and auscultation).
Secure tube to neck with suture after confirmation.
monitoring_requirements: Presence of CO2 return on monitoring equipment
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The size of the tracheostomy or endotracheal tube should not exceed an outer diameter of 8 mm, given the dimensions of the cricothyroid membrane.

clinical_guidelines.title: Rapid 4-Step Technique (RFST) for Cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: Perform from above the head of bed.
Make a horizontal stab incision through skin, subcutaneous tissues, and CT membrane simultaneously to gain airway access.
Stabilize larynx via hook against the cricoid cartilage.
Place the tracheostomy tube as described.
decision_points_and_pathways: Consider RFST for faster access but recognize higher complication rates (e.g., cricoid fractures) compared with standard technique in cadaveric models.
outcome_measures: Performed in about one-third the time required for the standard technique
Associated with a higher rate of complication, mainly cricoid fractures, in cadaveric models
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The RFST was performed in about one-third the time required to perform the standard technique.

clinical_guidelines.title: Percutaneous Cricothyroidotomy (Seldinger-based)
clinical_guidelines.condition: Emergency airway access via percutaneous cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: Make a small vertical skin incision over the CT membrane after identifying landmarks and fixing the larynx.
Introduce an 18-gauge needle attached to a syringe through the CT membrane; confirm with aspiration of air.
Insert a guide wire through the needle; remove the needle carefully.
Advance a cannula on a dilator over the guide wire into the airway; seat cannula against anterior neck.
Remove the dilator and guide wire.
decision_points_and_pathways: Use Seldinger technique steps (needle → wire → dilator/cannula) after landmark identification and stabilization.
monitoring_requirements: Aspiration of air to confirm needle placement
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Then, an 18-gauge needle attached to a syringe is introduced through the CT membrane, and proper positioning is conﬁrmed with aspiration of air.

clinical_guidelines.title: Postoperative Management After Cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: Examine airway by flexible endoscopy or formal bronchoscopy after surgical access is stabilized.
Perform postoperative chest x-ray to rule out pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.
Initiate standard tracheostomy tube hygiene: humidification, frequent cleaning of inner cannula, suctioning, monitoring cuff pressure, vigilant skin care.
Commonly convert to tracheostomy if access needed longer than 48–72 h.
decision_points_and_pathways: If an obvious reversible cause of obstruction is identified (e.g., foreign body), undertake appropriate action.
Consider conversion to tracheostomy based on expected duration of airway need.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Commonly, if access is needed for longer than 48–72 h, the cricothyroidotomy will be converted to tracheostomy.

clinical_guidelines.title: Use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound Prior to Cricothyroidotomy
specific_recommendations: Use handheld point-of-care ultrasound to define anatomy in the emergency setting.
Identify the cricothyroid membrane prior to cricothyroidotomy to potentially decrease complications.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Using point-of-care ultrasound can identify the cricothyroid membrane prior to cricothyroidotomy and potentially decrease complications.

definitions.content: Cricothyroidotomy is the creation of a surgical opening through the cricothyroid membrane and placement of a tube for ventilation.
definitions.source_excerpt: Cricothyroidotomy is the creation of a surgical opening through the cricothyroid membrane and placement of a tube for ventilation.

definitions.content: The rapid 4-step technique (RFST) for performing cricothyroidotomy was first described by Brofeldt and others as an attempt to simplify the procedure [7].

clinical_pearls.content: Cricothyroidotomy is the quickest and safest procedure to obtain an adequate airway in a patient in whom intubation has failed.
clinical_pearls.source_excerpt: Cricothyroidotomy is the quickest and safest procedure to obtain an adequate airway in a patient in whom intubation has failed.

clinical_pearls.content: After the CT membrane is carefully localized through the wound, a horizontal incision through the lower border is attempted to avoid injury to the superiorly positioned cricothyroid artery and vein.
